summary: Christophorus Becker (1875–1937) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He founded the Missionsärztliches Institut Würzburg in 1923, serving as a teacher there (~1922–1937), and was a Privatdozent for mission studies at the University of Würzburg (1925).

Chu-tsing Li (1920–2014) worked in sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Nanking (~1939–1943) and the University of Iowa (1947), later teaching art history at Iowa (~1955–1965) and joining the University of Kansas faculty in 1966.
Chuichi Kimura is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Minobusan University, attested as an associate professor in 2015 and as a former professor in 2026.

Chulthim Gurung is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at the University of British Columbia (2017–2019) and pursued a Ph.D. at McGill University (2019–2026), working as an assistant at both institutions.

Chun-i Tang (1909–1978) was a philosopher and sinologist. He studied under Shuming Liang, Jian Ouyang, Shili Xiong, and Thomé H. Fang at institutions including Peking University and National Central University, later holding chairs at CUHK (1963–1974) and New Asia Institute (~1953–1978).

Chun-min Yen works in Buddhist studies and sinology. Yen earned a PhD at the University of Arizona, studying under doctoral supervisor Robert M. Gimello, teacher Todd Brown, and traditional teachers Chanyun and Sheng Yen (attested 2004).
Chung-pui Tai is a scholar of linguistics, sinology, and Tibetology who studied at the Graduate School of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and held a post at the University of Hong Kong.

Chögyam Trungpa (1939–1987) worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He studied under Khenpo Gangshar, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, attended the University of Oxford (1963), and founded Naropa University and Kagyu Samye Ling.

Chökyi Gyatso studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, Khakyab Dorje, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and taught Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
Chökyi Nyima studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Dudjom Rinpoche.

Chökyi Nyima Rinpoche (born 1951) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Rumtek Monastery under the 16th Karmapa and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, founded the Rangjung Yeshe Institute (1981), and became abbot of Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling in 1976.
Chökyi Nyinche studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Shechen Gyaltsab, and taught Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.
Chönyi Drolma is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Thinley Norbu Rinpoche, Lama Tharchin Rinpoche, and Ngawang Zangpo (attested 2011).
Chüan-ying Yen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and history/archaeology. She earned a PhD from Harvard University, where she studied under John M. Rosenfield, Chu-tsing Li, and John Hay.

Chün-fang Yü (born 1938) works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. She studied at Columbia University (~1968–1973) and under Nanting and Sheng Yen, later teaching at Rutgers (~1972–2001) and Columbia (~2001–2013).

Claes Wennerberg (1939–1996) specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Gösta Liebert at the University of Gothenburg, earning a Ph.D. in 1981, and served there as docent and universitetslektor from ~1981 to 1996.

Claire Chang specializes in Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Sydney, Naropa University, and Nan Tien Institute, and served as Special Assistant to the Dean at Naropa University (2015–2019).

Clara Sue Kidwell (1941–2025) studied at the University of Oklahoma (Ph.D. ~1970). A historian, she held positions at UC Berkeley (~1974–1993), the National Museum of the American Indian, and directed programs at Oklahoma and UNC Chapel Hill.

Clare Carlisle (born 1977) is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. She studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (1995–2002) and held academic posts at the University of Liverpool (~2006–2011) and King's College London (~2012).

Clarence Herbert Hamilton (1886–1986) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his A.B. and Ph.D. at the University of Chicago, later serving as professor at Hartford Seminary (1928–1931) and Oberlin College (1931–1952).
